products.note: LLM app development platform; workflow orchestration; open-source; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Dify is a Chinese startup founded in 2023 that provides a no-code platform for building and deploying AI workflows, positioning developer tools as a layer between raw models and production deployment.

The platform sits in the middle of the AI stack. It abstracts model selection, data integration, and agent orchestration behind visual interfaces, which means teams can assemble AI applications without writing code. This matters because it lowers the technical bar for putting compute to work. If AI throughput depends on how many viable applications can be built against available models, then platforms that reduce engineering friction expand what that throughput can be.

The platform's deployment flexibility, offering cloud, private VPC, or self-hosted options, reflects a real constraint in the current market. Data sovereignty and regulatory requirements force builders to choose between vendor lock-in and operational complexity. That Dify supports multiple deployment targets suggests the platform recognizes this as a hard blocking issue for adoption, particularly outside the United States.

The data does not include customer count, usage volume, infrastructure costs, or which model providers dominate on the platform. It does not disclose whether Dify's own infrastructure requirements or model inference costs represent a meaningful fraction of its customers' total AI spend. Without that information, it is unclear whether the platform itself will become a compute or power constraint as it scales.

profile_text.body:
Dify is a for-profit startup founded in 2023 and headquartered in Suzhou, China that offers a platform for building and deploying AI-powered agentic workflows. The company describes itself as providing a single collaborative workspace where teams can construct agents, knowledge pipelines, models, and tools using visual building blocks and AI prompts, with deployment options spanning cloud, private VPC, or self-hosted environments. The platform supports retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, MCP integrations, and a marketplace of plugins, model providers, and data sources that can be reused across projects.

The site characterizes Dify as combining AI and machine learning capabilities on a no-code interface intended to make agent development accessible to non-specialists, and cites Volvo Cars as an example of an organization using the platform. The company notes that cross-border data review is advised for users of the product.

The held facts confirm Dify maintains a presence on theworldofai.org and is tracked under the Coding and Developer Tools category as an open-source LLM application development platform. No litigation, SEC filings, or patent records are held for the company at this time.
